title: OpenAI Rehires Thinking Machines Co-Founder Days After Startup Exit
excerpt: Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng has stepped down from the AI startup, citing health concerns and the demands of startup life, before quickly returni...
content_html:
Caroline Ryan

Sun, August 2, 2026 at 10:30 AM EDT 5 min read

Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng has stepped down from the AI startup, citing health concerns and the demands of startup life, before quickly returning to OpenAI. 

"I don't feel I'm able to continue at the pace a startup requires. After thinking about it for several months, I have to ultimately admit that the amount of consistent stress and workload have pushed me beyond what my health can sustain physicallly," Weng wrote in a post on X.

Earlier this week, OpenAI confirmed Weng's rehire to TechCrunch, adding that she will be leading a new research team focused on accelerating the company's internal AI research.  The team will focus on research into recursive self-improvement, a process where AI systems improve their own capabilities through repeated iterations.

Weng previously worked at OpenAI for more than six years, holding several roles during her time at the company including research scientist, head of applied AI research, head of safety systems and finally VP of research, safety, a role she remained in until 2024, when she left for Thinking Labs, according to her LinkedIn profile.

Thinking Machines co-founder and former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati responded to Weng's post on X, voicing support for her decision to focus on her health. 

"We'll miss you, it's been wonderful building Thinky together. I'm glad that you're putting you're health first. Thank you for everything," Murati wrote under Weng's post. Whether Murati was aware that Weng would ultimately rejoin OpenAI remains unclear.

OpenAI Adds Talent

This is not the first time OpenAI has recruited talent from rival companies to strengthen its team.

Last month, Liz Wamai joined OpenAI as head of recruiting after more than three years at Netflix, as well as former Uber Technologies India and South Asia President Prabhjeet Singh as its managing director for the country.

White House artificial intelligence adviser Dean Ball also joined OpenAI, in a role focused on  shaping frontier AI policy.

The ChatGPT maker has also added 40 employees from Salesforce since the start of the year, as the company plans to double its workforce from 4,500 to 8,000 by the end of 2026, the Financial Times reported.

Thinking Machines 联合创始人 Lilian Weng 以健康问题和创业生活的需求为由，从这家人工智能初创公司辞职，然后迅速返回 OpenAI。

“我觉得我无法继续按照初创公司所需的速度进行。 经过几个月的思考，我最终不得不承认，持续的压力和工作量已经让我超出了身体健康所能承受的范围，”翁在 X 上的一篇帖子中写道。

不要错过：

  • 一次糟糕的招聘可能会让一家初创企业倒退数年。 以下是创始人最常误判的 5 名员工——以及原因

本周早些时候，OpenAI 确认 Weng 重新受雇于 TechCrunch，并补充说她将领导一个新的研究团队，专注于加速公司内部的人工智能研究。 该团队将重点研究递归自我改进，这是人工智能系统通过反复迭代提高自身能力的过程。

Weng 此前在 OpenAI 工作了六年多，在公司期间担任过多个职位，包括研究科学家、应用人工智能研究负责人、安全系统负责人，最后是安全研究副总裁，根据她的 LinkedIn 个人资料，她一直担任这一职位直到 2024 年，当时她离开到 Thinking Labs。

Thinking Machines 联合创始人、前 OpenAI 首席技术官 Mira Murati 在 X 上回复了翁的帖子，表示支持她关注健康的决定。

“我们会想念你的，一起打造 Thinky 真是太棒了。 我很高兴你把健康放在第一位。 谢谢你所做的一切，”穆拉蒂在翁的帖子下写道。 目前尚不清楚 Murati 是否知道 Weng 最终会重新加入 OpenAI。

趋势：避免第一大投资错误：你的“安全”持仓可能会让你付出巨大的代价

OpenAI 增添人才

这并不是 OpenAI 第一次从竞争对手公司招募人才来加强其团队。

上个月，在 Netflix 工作三年多后，Liz Wamai 加入 OpenAI 担任招聘主管，前 Uber Technologies 印度和南亚总裁 Prabhjeet Singh 担任该国董事总经理。

白宫人工智能顾问 Dean Ball 也加入了 OpenAI，主要负责制定前沿人工智能政策。

据英国《金融时报》报道，自今年年初以来，ChatGPT 制造商还从 Salesforce 增加了 40 名员工，该公司计划到 2026 年底将员工人数从 4,500 人增加一倍至 8,000 人。
